Read the design. Rebuild it.

  1. Read the structure

    The input has no labels. Size, position and grouping tell it which piece is the headline, logo, product and button.

  2. Try real layouts

    A column, a side-by-side split, three columns or a single row, each in the original reading order.

  3. Measure and score

    Text is measured with the official renderer's fonts. Each layout is scored on readability, hierarchy, collisions and space.

  4. Pick and explain

    The best layout wins, and every decision is recorded so you can see why.

Run it

The challenge scores every entry in the starter's Python Docker image, so the engine is Python. Run it in Docker the way stage one does, or straight from a virtual environment.

Offline, with no network, like stage one.

$ docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t chameleon-engine .
$ docker run --rm --network none \
    -v $(pwd)/input:/app/input -v $(pwd)/output:/app/output chameleon-engine

Python 3.10 or newer, inside the starter repo.

$ pip install -r requirements.txt
$ python -m engine.main      # resize every task in input/
$ python -m studio.server    # demo UI on http://127.0.0.1:8765

Limits

  • Long copy stays smallEvery element stays visible and copy is never rewritten, so very long copy gets small type on tiny banners.
  • Roles are inferredThe engine reads roles from size and position. An unusual design can be misread, and the result is then plainer.
  • Our numbersThe figures above come from our own checks, not Adobe's scorer.
